P1.evidence: Referenced the setter without reading anything back — "Yeah, he kind of gave me an overview of where you're at." Frame was two-part, not four: "I do want to go a little bit deeper, really build out what it is that you want. And then, yeah, if the coaching aligns, we can talk about it. If not, that's fine as well. Alrighty?" Got agreement ("Wonderful") and opened correctly: "what was it that you were hoping that we could potentially help you with?"

P2.evidence: Baseline was almost entirely skipped. No age, height or weight asked — age 40 was volunteered ("I didn't want to create any hindrances in my 40 year old body"). No health-conditions question at all, despite the prospect volunteering a near-faint. No injury or movement-limitation question. Work was asked socially ("what do you coach out of curiosity?") but not for desk-bound vs on-feet. Training history partially covered via "Have you been doing any kettlebell stuff?" Diet never asked. Sleep was asked properly: "what would you say your sleep is like?" Energy never asked. The rep openly deferred the whole baseline to onboarding: "he's going to be very specific and tangible in terms of numbers... How much do you weigh? How tall are you?"

P3.evidence: Asked the six-month physical picture — "six months down the line, where do you want to be at with it physically?" — and the prospect refused to set a goal. The rep let it go rather than reframing. The basketball goal was volunteered, never asked for. The deep bridge was attempted through a spiritual variant ("if you were to picture the whole most perfect version of you... what do you think he would say?"), which is a partial substitute. Never asked what moving better does for him, never asked who else it impacts, and never drove to kids, marriage or legacy — despite the prospect having a wife and children on the table. Reflected back well: "This is what I'm sensing. Let me know if this is right" and the prospect corrected him, which the rep absorbed.

P4.evidence: Strongest phase. Root cause was pursued early and hard: "What typically holds you back, do you think, from actually sticking to something?" and "is that something in your life which is just with fitness? Or... do you notice that happen with other things?" The prospect named the gap himself — ego, self-sabotage, no accountability, being unable to coach himself. Past attempts were only loosely mapped (gym machines, COVID training, one kettlebell dabble) and never sequenced. The 'information isn't the problem' line was never run even though the prospect handed it over: "there's a lot of videos on youtube and a lot of pdf guides... it's probably not a rocket science to do kettlebells."

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was never run. No two-year question, no 'willing to settle', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The rep moved from root cause straight into a philosophy pitch: "Well, if you feel like you're ready to make that change... I'm fine with walking you through kind of what the coaching looks like." With no cost of inaction established, the later hesitation had nothing to push against.

P6.evidence: No commitment check before presenting. The belief question only appeared after the price, as objection handling: "money aside, do you feel like we can actually get you to where you want to go?" — and the prospect's answer was hedged ("you cannot get me where I want to go, I need to go there"). The 'any reason you wouldn't go all in' question was never asked, and the rep presented the offer without a clear yes in hand.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted, so the phase applies. No payment collected, no payment link sent, no Trevor onboarding call booked, no agreement email, no Skool link or questionnaire. The rep offered to compress it ("if you let me know that you're ready, I can send you all the onboarding stuff on WhatsApp, and then we can book in your call with Trevor for Monday or Tuesday") and the prospect declined: "for me, it's not a hurry." The rep accepted immediately.

objection_plays.detail: "This is definitely something I got to think about." The rep did not run the OA sequence when it landed — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'that man you want to be — how does HE decide right now'. Ten minutes later he did ask 'what do you feel like really is the thing that's holding you back... where do you feel like that comes from?', which is the OA probe arriving late and alone.

"my wife is also part of the company holder I would have to ask her." The rep ran most of the play cleanly: isolated with 'money aside do you feel like we can actually get you to where you want to go', asked her name ("I don't want to call her your wife"), asked what she would say to the €5,100 through the business, and ran the permission-vs-FYI frame ("is it more of like a, hey, just letting you know... or is it like a permission thing"). Not run: 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger', and the deposit-with-refund fallback.

"Is there some negotiation space in there? In terms of, like, the price?" The rep held price without flinching — "No, the price is the price. It is what it is" — which is the right instinct and the best moment of the call. But none of the OC play ran: no isolate, no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no payment-plan mention, no financial picture at all. The rep never established whether the prospect could actually pay, and the prospect's own volunteered signal ("I also take the same money from my clients") did the work instead.

The rep proactively probed for fear rather than waiting for it, running the plane variant almost verbatim: "have you ever been skydiving before?... the hard part is always jumping out the plane." Followed with 'I wanted to make sure that you weren't making this important decision through fear' and the two-types-of-people frame. The prospect closed it out ("the fear is the fear of losing or failing, but I don't have this anymore").

Script gap. The prospect's stated blocker was neither money, spouse, timing, doubt nor deliberation-as-avoidance — it was a professed need to make the decision alone and somatically: "I want to take the time for myself to feed it through and to feel this connection... I'm not going to make this step now once I haven't tiled it through in myself." He is himself a coach and explicitly named and rejected closing pressure ("they're still like, you know, trying to do all these closing techniques"). The playbook has no path for a prospect who is decision-competent, non-resistant, and simply will not decide on a call. The rep, correctly, stopped pushing — but had nothing to convert with.

Second script gap. The live anchor was Primal's own Primal University email — "it was reduced from 1,999 to 1,000 euros per year" — sitting next to a €5,100 six-month price. The rep differentiated on support and feedback, which was adequate, but there is no scripted play for handling the company's own low-ticket product surfacing mid-close.

notes: The rep is genuinely good at rapport and root cause and held price without blinking, but he ran the back half of the call before the front half: baseline skipped, consequence frame never run, and the offer presented with no commitment check. With no cost of inaction on the table there was nothing to bring the prospect back to when he asked for a night to think. Coach the sequence, not the warmth — and P2 medical questions are non-optional given what this prospect volunteered.
